territorial_scope.description: Applies to the Department of Defense and to recipients of its financial assistance, which must be based in the United States.

evidence.quote: No financial assistance authorized in this section shall be awarded to an entity outside of the United States.

summary.short: The bill would authorize the Secretary of Defense to establish at least one National Security and Defense Artificial Intelligence Institute at a senior military college and award it competitive, five-year financial assistance, renewable once, for AI research, testbeds, data sets and workforce development. Recipients must be US-based.
summary.long: The bill, titled the GUARD Act, would authorize the Secretary of Defense to establish at least one National Security and Defense Artificial Intelligence Institute at an eligible host institution, defined as a senior military college under 10 U.S.C. 2111a(f). An Institute would be an AI research institute focused on cross-cutting or foundational science for national security and defense, building partnerships among public and private organizations and supporting interdisciplinary research and workforce development. The Secretary may seek to award financial assistance to a host institution or consortia for uses including curated data sets for training and testing AI systems, testbeds for evaluation before deployment, computing and data access, technical assistance and outreach. Awards run for five years, may be renewed once for up to five more, require an application, and follow a competitive merit-based review. Recipients and subgrantees must be based in the United States. The bill contains no separate penalties or enforcement provisions and states no effective date; it is at the introduced stage.

notes: Bill text as introduced; no enacting-clause date, appropriation amount or operative effective date is stated. Provisions are largely permissive ('may establish', 'may seek to award'). Sec. 2(c)(4) reads 'A eligible host institution' and Sec. 2(c)(2)(G) reads 'as may determined', as written. Sec. 2(b) describes institute characteristics without imposing duties on named addressees.
